Lie on your back with one foot planted. Hold a padded light kettlebell securely over your hips. Lift without twisting or arching, lower, and complete the same repetitions on the other leg.
Use secured upper-back support and a loo: Use secured support under your upper back and a loop above knees. Lift hips without arching.
Use secured upper-back support. Hold the: Use secured support under your upper back. Hold the padded bag across hips and lift with control.
From hands and knees, lift one bent leg: From hands and knees, lift one bent leg behind you without arching your back. Switch sides.
Place a loop band around your thighs jus: Place a loop band around your thighs just above your knees. From hands and knees, keep one knee bent and move that thigh backward and slightly upward, without arching your back. Return with control and complete both sides of your body.
Use a secure low anchor and ankle strap. Hold support and extend the hip gently. Switch sides.
Use a low pulley and ankle strap. Keep y: Use a low pulley and ankle strap. Keep your pelvis steady and extend the hip. Switch sides.
Lie face down with one knee bent. Lift t: Lie face down with one knee bent. Lift the thigh slightly without arching. Complete both sides of your body.
Plant feet slightly wider than hips. Lif: Plant feet slightly wider than hips. Lift your pelvis without letting your knees cave inward.
Lift hips from the floor and pause for t: Lift hips from the floor and pause for two seconds at the top before lowering.
Hold a padded light weight over hips, so: Hold a padded light weight over hips, soles together. Use a small controlled hip lift.
Sit tall on a stable seat with a loop ab: Sit tall on a stable seat with a loop above knees. Open knees without rocking your trunk.
Use a low pulley and ankle strap. Hold s: Use a low pulley and ankle strap. Hold support, move the leg sideways and switch sides.
Place a loop above your knees. Keep hips: Place a loop above your knees. Keep hips stacked and lift the top leg slowly. Switch sides.
Use a loop above knees. Lift one bent kn: Use a loop above knees. Lift one bent knee sideways with a steady pelvis. Switch sides.
Place a loop band above your knees, soft: Place a loop band above your knees, soften your knees and take short diagonal forward steps without letting your knees cave inward. Count each step as one repetitionetition; log the total across both feet.
Place a loop band above your knees and s: Place a loop band above your knees and soften your knees. Take small diagonal backward steps in a clear space, keeping tension in the band. Each step is one repetitionetition; count both feet together.
Hold a wall. Bring one leg gently across: Hold a wall. Bring one leg gently across the midline without leaning. Complete both sides of your body.
Lie on your side with the top foot plant: Lie on your side with the top foot planted in front. Lift the lower leg gently. Switch sides.
Use a low pulley and ankle strap. Draw t: Use a low pulley and ankle strap. Draw the working leg across your body without twisting. Switch sides.
Use a secure low side anchor and ankle s: Use a secure low side anchor and ankle strap. Draw the leg inward without leaning. Switch sides.
Lie on your side with knees bent togethe: Lie on your side with knees bent together. Raise the top foot without separating knees. Switch sides.
Sit on a stable seat. Keep knees in plac: Sit on a stable seat. Keep knees in place and move one foot outward gently. Switch sides.
Lie on your side with hips stacked. Lift: Lie on your side with hips stacked. Lift the top leg slightly and make six small controlled circles each way. Repeat on the other side. One complete circle is one repetitionetition; log 24 circles in total.
Use a secure low anchor and ankle strap. Lift one knee without leaning back. Complete both sides of your body.
Hold a wall, soften the standing knee an: Hold a wall, soften the standing knee and lift the heel. Complete both sides of your body.
Hold one weight and support with your fr: Hold one weight and support with your free hand. Raise and lower on one foot. Switch sides.
Hold the bell by your side and use suppo: Hold the kettlebell by your side and use support. Lift one heel slowly and complete both sides of your body.
Hug the bag securely. Rise onto both for: Hug the bag securely. Rise onto both forefeet and lower slowly near stable support.
Stand securely on a long band under the: Stand securely on a long band under the balls of both feet and hold its ends by your sides with gentle tension. Raise your heels slowly and lower under control. If balancing with the band is awkward, choose a supported bodyweight calf raise.
Sit on a stable seat. Hold a padded bell: Sit on a stable seat. Hold a padded kettlebell above one knee and lift that heel. Switch sides.
Sit on a stable seat. Hold the bag acros: Sit on a stable seat. Hold the bag across thighs above knees and raise both heels.
Sit on a stable seat. Lift one heel with: Sit on a stable seat. Lift one heel with the knee bent and switch sides.
Hold a padded weight above one bent knee: Hold a padded weight above one bent knee. Lift the heel with control and switch sides.
Use a light weight and stable support. K: Use a light weight and stable support. Keep knees softly bent as you lift both heels.
Hold a light bell and use support. Keep: Hold a light kettlebell and use support. Keep knees bent while raising and lowering heels.
Hold support and pause two seconds at th: Hold support and pause two seconds at the top of each heel raise before lowering.
Hold support, raise both heels, then low: Hold support, raise both heels, then lower for three seconds without bouncing.
Lean hands against a wall with a straigh: Lean hands against a wall with a straight body. Raise heels while keeping toes planted.
Use a wall for support. Load the front f: Use a wall for support. Load the front foot and raise that heel. Complete both sides of your body.
Hold one weight and support with the fre: Hold one weight and support with the free hand. Raise the front heel, then switch sides.
Step one foot sideways while raising you: Step one foot sideways while raising your arms, then return to the starting position. Alternate sides without jumping. One step out and back is one repetitionetition; log the total across both sides of your body.
Start with feet together and arms by you: Start with feet together and arms by your sides. Jump feet apart as arms rise, then return. Land softly with knees aligned; one out-and-back cycle is one repetition. Choose Step Jacks for no jumping.
March in place with an upright torso and: March in place with an upright torso and controlled knee lifts. Alternate sides.
Bring one knee toward the opposite hand: Bring one knee toward the opposite hand without pulling on your neck. Alternate sides.
Use light controlled punches with soft k: Use light controlled punches with soft knees. Count each punch and avoid snapping elbows.
Squat through a comfortable range, stand: Squat through a comfortable range, stand and lift heels with control.
Step back into a high plank, then step f: Step back into a high plank, then step forward and stand. No jump or push-up is required.
Step sideways and lightly tap the other: Step sideways and lightly tap the other foot behind without jumping. Keep your knee aligned with the stepping foot. One sideways step and tap is one repetitionetition; count both directions together.
From a high plank step one foot sideways: From a high plank step one foot sideways and return. Alternate sides with hips steady.
Begin on hands and knees, then lift knee: Begin on hands and knees, then lift knees just off the floor. Move one hand and the opposite foot forward together, then the other pair. Each paired movement is one step; count the total steps.
Hold weights by your sides. March uprigh: Hold weights by your sides. March upright without swaying and count each step.
Hold the bell at your chest and march wi: Hold the kettlebell at your chest and march without leaning backward. Count each step.
Hug the bag close and march with hips le: Hug the bag close and march with hips level. Count each step.
Place a light loop band over the midfoot: Place a light loop band over the midfoot of both shoes and stand tall. Lift one knee, lower it, then alternate without leaning backward. Each knee lift is one step; log the total across both legs.
Use light dumbbells. Squat through a com: Use light dumbbells. Squat through a comfortable range, stand fully, then lift the weights in front to shoulder height and lower them. One squat followed by one raise is one repetition.
Use a secured bench and correctly set ra: Use a secured bench and correctly set rack safety arms or a spotter. Keep feet firmly on the floor, lower the bar under control and press without bouncing.
Use a stable bench. Keep wrists stacked,: Use a stable bench. Keep wrists stacked, lower through a comfortable range and press with control.
Lie on your back with knees bent and one: Lie on your back with knees bent and one kettlebell in each hand. Stack wrists above elbows, lower both upper arms gently to the floor and press up without bouncing. One press with both arms is one repetition.
Begin with two manageable kettlebells ra: Begin with two manageable kettlebells supported at your shoulders. Tense your abdominal muscles, press both overhead without leaning back, then lower to the position at your shoulders. One simultaneous press is one repetition.
Rack one manageable kettlebell at each s: Hold one manageable kettlebell supported at each shoulder. Press one overhead while keeping the other supported, lower and alternate. Complete the target on both arms and log each arm press once.
Hold a kettlebell in each hand, hinge at: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, bend at your hips and Tense your abdominal muscles your trunk. Pull both kettlebells toward your lower ribs without sudden movements, then lower. One Pull with both arms is one repetition.
Rack two manageable kettlebells at your: Hold two manageable kettlebells supported at your shoulders with elbows close. Keep heels planted, squat through a controlled range and stand tall. One squat is one repetition.
Hold one kettlebell by each side. Step o: Hold one kettlebell by each side of your body. Step one foot back, bend both knees through a comfortable range and return. Alternate legs and log each return to standing as one repetition.
Hold two kettlebells in front of your th: Hold two kettlebells in front of your thighs. Soften knees, push hips back and lower the kettlebells close to your legs. Stand by extending your hips without leaning back.
Set two kettlebells beside your feet. Hi: Set two kettlebells beside your feet. bend at the hips and bend knees enough to grip them, Tense your abdominal muscles and stand with the weights close. Lower both kettlebells under control before the next rep.
Hold a manageable kettlebell by each sid: Hold a manageable kettlebell by each side of your body. Stand tall and march without swaying. Each knee lift is one step; log the combined total across both legs.
Rack a manageable kettlebell at each sho: Hold a manageable kettlebell supported at each shoulder. Keep ribs over hips and march slowly without leaning back. Each knee lift is one step; count both legs together.
Hold one light kettlebell by each side of your body. Raise both heels, pause and lower with control. If you need a free hand for support, choose the single-kettlebell version instead.
Begin with two light kettlebells in a se: Begin with two light kettlebells in a secure position with the weights supported at the shoulders. Squat, stand and use that leg drive to press overhead. Lower to the position at your shoulders before the next squat. One squat followed by one press is one repetition.
Hold one light kettlebell by its handle: Hold one light kettlebell by its handle in each hand, palms inward. Keep upper arms by your sides, curl both with control and lower without swinging the weight. One simultaneous curl is one repetition.
Place one whole foot on a low, stable ex: Place one whole foot on a low, stable exercise step. Push through that foot to stand on the step, then step down with control. Finish the target leading with each leg. One ascent and controlled return is one repetitionetition; use a platform, not an unstable chair.
Hold weights by your sides and place one: Hold weights by your sides and place one whole foot on a low, stable step. Stand through the leading leg without jumping, then step down slowly. Complete the target leading with each leg.
Hold one kettlebell at your chest. Step: Hold one kettlebell at your chest. Step onto a low, stable platform with the whole leading foot, stand and lower with control. Complete the target on each leading leg.
Hold one manageable kettlebell by each s: Hold one manageable kettlebell by each side of your body. Step onto a low, stable platform without jumping, stand and lower slowly. Complete both leading legs and count each ascent and return as one repetition.
Stand beside a low, stable step. Place t: Stand beside a low, stable step. Place the nearer foot fully on it, push through that leg to stand, then lower slowly. Turn around to work the other side. One ascent and return is one repetition.
Hold light dumbbells by your sides and s: Hold light dumbbells by your sides and stand beside a low, stable platform. Step up through the nearer leg, then lower slowly. Complete the target on both sides of your body without bouncing off the floor.
Stand on a low, stable step. Keep one fo: Stand on a low, stable step. Keep one foot planted on it and bend that knee slowly until the opposite heel lightly touches the floor. Push through the standing leg to return. Complete both sides of your body.
Hold light weights on a low, stable step: Hold light weights on a low, stable step. Keep one foot planted, lower the opposite heel toward the floor and return through the standing leg without dropping onto the other foot. Complete both sides of your body.
Slide your back down a sturdy wall with: Slide your back down a sturdy wall with feet slightly forward. Hold a manageable knee bend, keep feet flat and breathe steadily. Stand when done. Log seconds held, not repetitions.
Hold one light dumbbell close to your ch: Hold one light dumbbell close to your chest with both hands. Lean your back against a sturdy wall and hold a comfortable knee bend with feet flat. Log seconds held; put the weight down under control before standing if needed.
Hold one light kettlebell at your chest. With your back against a sturdy wall, hold a manageable knee bend and breathe. Log the seconds you hold, not repetitions.
Sit on a stable seat with a band attache: Sit on a stable seat with a band attached to a secure low anchor behind you and an ankle strap on one leg. Keeping your thigh supported, straighten that knee through a comfortable range, then bend it slowly. Complete both sides of your body. This isolates the quads more than a squat.
Sit on a stable seat in front of a low p: Sit on a stable seat in front of a low pulley behind you, with an ankle strap on one leg. Keep the thigh supported as you straighten the knee, then return slowly. Complete both sides of your body. This is quad isolation rather than a whole-leg squat movement.
Kneel tall with knees about hip-width ap: Kneel tall with knees about hip-width apart and toes relaxed or tucked comfortably. Keep hips extended and torso in line with thighs, lean back a small controlled distance from the knees, then return. Do not fold at your hips; start with a short range.
Sit near the front of a sturdy seat with: Sit near the front of a sturdy seat with feet firmly on the floor. Lean forward slightly, push through your feet to stand fully, then sit down with control. One stand and return is one repetition.
Set a secured adjustable bench to a mode: Set a secured adjustable bench to a modest incline (about 15–30 degrees). Sit with dumbbells on your thighs and position them above your upper chest as you lie back. Plant your feet, lower with wrists above elbows, then press up without bouncing. Use weights you can safely position and put down.
Secure an incline bench inside a rack wi: Secure an incline bench inside a rack with safety arms set to catch the bar below your controlled range. Lift the bar off the rack supports above your upper chest, lower without bouncing and press up. Keep your feet firmly on the floor and use a spotter where appropriate.
Lie on a firm exercise bench with feet p: Lie on a firm exercise bench with feet firmly on the floor and light dumbbells above your chest. Keep elbows softly bent as you open your arms, stopping at a comfortable chest stretch. Bring the weights back above your chest without changing the elbow bend or bouncing.
Use stable parallel bars. Support your w: Use stable parallel bars. Support your weight with arms straight, bend your elbows to lower through a comfortable range, then press back up. Keep shoulders controlled and avoid dropping into the bottom. Choose a supported push-up if you cannot perform controlled repetitions.
Fix one end of the bar securely in a pur: Fix one end of the bar securely in a purpose-built landmine attachment. Stand in a split stance facing the free end and hold it near one shoulder. Tense your abdominal muscles and press forward and upward along the bar’s arc, then lower slowly. Complete both sides of your body; do not wedge a loose bar into a wall.
Use a secure pull-up bar with an overhan: Use a secure pull-up bar with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width. Start from a controlled hang, draw elbows down and pull until your chin clears the bar without craning your neck. Lower under control. Avoid kipping or swinging; choose pulldowns if a controlled rep is not yet available.
Grip a secure bar with palms facing you: Grip a secure bar with palms facing you at a comfortable width. From a controlled hang, pull your elbows down until your chin clears the bar, then lower slowly. Keep your torso controlled without swinging the weight or forcing your neck forward.
Use a fixed low bar rated for bodyweight: Use a fixed low bar rated for bodyweight rows. Hold it overhand with heels on the floor and your body in a straight line. Pull your chest toward the bar, then lower slowly. Bend your knees for an easier angle. Do not use a loose bar resting on open rack hooks.
Set a secured bench to an incline that l: Set a secured bench to an incline that lets the weights hang freely. Lie chest-down with feet firmly on the floor. Pull both dumbbells toward your lower ribs without lifting your chest from the pad, then lower under control.
Secure the bar in a landmine and attach: Secure the bar in a landmine and attach a rated T-bar handle near the loaded end. Stand with one foot on each side of your body of the bar, bend at the hips and tense your abdominal muscles. Pull the handle toward your lower chest, then lower without rounding or jerking your torso.
Lie lengthwise on a firm exercise bench: Lie lengthwise on a firm exercise bench with head supported and feet firmly on the floor. Hold one light dumbbell securely above your chest with both hands. Keep elbows softly bent and ribs controlled as you lower it behind your head, then bring it back above your chest. Stop before your back arches.
Sit against a modestly inclined backrest: Sit against a modestly inclined backrest with dumbbells hanging at your sides. Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows to lift the weight without rolling the shoulders forward. Lower slowly through a comfortable elbow range; avoid forcing the arms backward.
Sit at a preacher bench with your upper: Sit at a preacher bench with your upper arm fully supported on the pad and one light dumbbell in hand. Lift the weight by bending your elbows without lifting your upper arm, then lower slowly without forcing the elbow straight. Complete both sides of your body.
Use a firm exercise bench and rack with: Use a firm exercise bench and rack with correctly set safety arms. Grip near shoulder width, not with hands touching. Lower toward your lower chest with elbows comfortably close to your sides, then press without bouncing. Keep wrists above forearms.
Set rack hooks below shoulder height and: Set rack hooks below shoulder height and safety arms just below your intended squat depth. Place the bar on your upper-back muscles, not your neck, Lift the bar off the rack supports and Tense your abdominal muscles. Squat with feet firmly on the floor and knees tracking with toes, then stand without losing trunk position. Use a depth and load you control.
Set up inside a rack with safety arms. R: Set up inside a rack with safety arms. Rest the bar on the fronts of your shoulders with elbows raised and a comfortable supported grip. Lift the bar off the rack supports, Tense your abdominal muscles and squat while keeping your chest and elbows up, then stand. Choose goblet squats if you cannot hold a stable position with the weights supported at the shoulders.
Stand in front of a low, secured exercis: Stand in front of a low, secured exercise bench and place the top of one foot on it behind you. Keep most weight over the front foot. Bend the front knee to lower with control, then stand through that leg. Use a manageable rear-foot height and complete both sides of your body.
Adjust the seat and safety stops on the: Adjust the seat and safety stops on the machine. Place feet securely on the platform and release the safeties as instructed by the manufacturer. Bend your knees only while your pelvis stays against the pad, then press without snapping knees straight. Re-engage the safeties before leaving.
Adjust the seat so your knees line up wi: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine pivot and the roller rests above your ankles. Keep thighs on the seat, straighten your knees through a comfortable range, then lower slowly without kicking or swinging.
Start with a loaded bar over your midfoo: Start with a loaded bar over your midfoot at standard plate height; use stable blocks if the plates are too small. bend at the hips and bend knees to grip just outside your legs. Tense your abdominal muscles, keep the bar close and push through the floor to stand. Finish tall without leaning back, then bend at the hips and bend knees to set it down under control.
Set the bar at standard plate height. Ta: Set the bar at standard plate height. Take a comfortable wide stance with toes turned out and grip the bar with your hands between your legs. Tense your abdominal muscles, keep knees tracking with toes and stand with the bar close. Lower under control; do not force a wider stance than your hips allow.
Stand centered inside a loaded trap bar: Stand centered inside a loaded trap bar on a level floor. bend at the hips and bend knees to grip the handles, Tense your abdominal muscles and stand with even pressure through both feet. Lower under control. Use the raised handles if needed and do not jerk the bar from the floor.
Unrack a light bar across your upper-bac: Lift the bar off the rack supports a light bar across your upper-back muscles inside a rack with safety arms. Keep knees softly bent, Tense your abdominal muscles and push your hips backward while the torso tips forward. Stop while your spine stays controlled, then extend your hips to stand. Begin lighter than a squat.
Secure a firm exercise bench so it canno: Secure a firm exercise bench so it cannot slide. Rest your upper back on the edge and position a padded bar across your hips using a load you can position and remove safely. Plant your feet and lift until your torso and thighs align, then lower. Keep your ribcage above your pelvis without arching your lower back and avoid arching your back.
Adjust the machine so knees line up with: Adjust the machine so knees line up with its pivot and the roller sits above your heels. Lie against the pad, bend your knees to curl the roller upward, then lower slowly. Keep hips against the pad and avoid lifting your pelvis.
Align your knees with the machine pivot,: Align your knees with the machine pivot, place the lower roller above your heels and secure the thigh pad. Draw your heels back under the seat by bending your knees, then extend slowly. Keep your back and thighs supported.
Lie on your back with heels on exercise: Lie on your back with heels on exercise sliders or towels on a suitable smooth floor. Lift into a low bridge. Slide your heels away only as far as you can keep hips controlled, then draw them back. Start with short slides; one out-and-back movement is one repetition.
Kneel on a padded surface with ankles he: Kneel on a padded surface with ankles held by a purpose-built, securely fixed Nordic anchor. Keep hips extended and torso aligned with thighs. Lower forward slowly from the knees, catch yourself with your hands and use your arms to help reset. Begin with a short, assisted range. This is a hamstring exercise, unlike the backward-leaning reverse Nordic.
Adjust the machine pads and safety stops: Adjust the machine pads and safety stops for your height. Place the balls of your feet securely on its platform, keeping knees softly unlocked. Raise your heels, pause, then lower through a comfortable ankle range without bouncing. Use the handles for balance.
Lie on your back with hands lightly supp: Lie on your back with hands lightly supporting your head and knees bent above your hips. Lift your shoulder blades and rotate one shoulder toward the opposite knee as the other leg extends. Alternate slowly without pulling your neck. Each turn to one side is one repetitionetition; log both sides of your body together.
Hang from a secure bar with shoulders co: Hang from a secure bar with shoulders controlled. Bend your knees and curl them toward your chest with a small pelvic tilt, then lower slowly. Avoid swinging or just kicking your thighs upward. Choose reverse crunches if grip or hanging control limits you.

Hang from a secure bar with shoulders controlled. Raise your legs in front through a range you control, adding a gentle pelvic curl rather than swinging. Lower slowly. Keep knees softly bent if needed and choose knee raises for a shorter lever.
Attach a rope to a high pulley. Kneel fa: Attach a rope to a high pulley. Kneel facing the stack and hold the rope beside your temples without pulling your neck. Curl your ribs toward your pelvis while keeping hips mostly still, then return slowly. Use a load that lets your trunk move rather than just sitting back.
Stand side-on to a high pulley with feet: Stand side-on to a high pulley with feet firmly on the floor comfortably. Hold the handle with both hands and draw it diagonally toward the opposite hip, allowing your feet and hips to turn with your torso. Return slowly, then reverse your stance for the other side. Avoid twisting against fixed knees.
Hold a manageable dumbbell by each side: Hold a manageable dumbbell by each side of your body and stand tall. Walk in a clear, level space with short controlled steps, shoulders relaxed and torso steady. Set the weights down under control. Log walking seconds, not steps or meters.
Hold one dumbbell beside your hip and wa: Hold one dumbbell beside your hip and walk in a clear, level space without leaning toward or away from it. Set it down under control and repeat holding it on the other side. Log the combined walking seconds for both sides of your body.
Practice the full sequence without weigh: Practice the full sequence without weight first and use a light kettlebell only once it is familiar. Lie on your back with the working arm vertical and that knee bent. Roll onto the opposite forearm, press to the hand, lift hips and sweep the straight leg behind into a half-kneeling position. Straighten your torso and stand while keeping the kettlebell stable overhead. Reverse the sequence to lie down. One rise and return is one repetitionetition; complete both sides of your body. Learn the transitions before adding load.
Lie beside a low, secured exercise bench: Lie beside a low, secured exercise bench with your top knee supported on it and your elbow below your shoulder. Lift hips into a side plank and bring the lower leg toward the supported leg. Hold with hips level, then lower. Repeat on the other side and log combined seconds. Keep the knee-supported short lever; do not begin with the ankle-supported version.
